findings.scenario: Job is Zod-parsed then handed to propose as Object.freeze({ job, input, signal }) (shallow). input is deep-frozen; job is not. propose can do job.inputSha256 = '0'*64; job.jobId = 'job-other'; return { summary: 'Bounded proposal' }. Execution still returns status complete whose jobId/inputSha256/jobSha256 follow the mutated copy, so tampering receives complete.
findings.remediation: Deep-freeze a clone of the parsed job (cloneAndFreezeJson) before invokeBoundedProposal and build every receipt only from that frozen snapshot.

findings.scenario: Receipts come from AiTeammateRunReceiptV1Schema.parse; .readonly() is not a runtime freeze. Only the { proposal, receipt } wrapper is Object.freeze'd. After a failed/cancelled/budget-exhausted return, result.receipt.status/outputSha256/stoppingCondition can be assigned in place (ES module strict throw only if the receipt object itself were frozen). Emitted receipts are not immutable.
findings.remediation: Deep-freeze every parsed receipt (cloneAndFreezeJson or Object.freeze of receipt and effectClasses) before returning.

findings.scenario: Binding checks jobSha256, jobId, teammateId, inputSha256, effectClasses, outputSchemaId, executionLane. A complete receipt with a swapped outputSha256 (or any 64-hex digest) still validates. Tampered output hashes are accepted as bound complete receipts.
findings.remediation: Require the canonical output digest as an argument (or null for non-complete) and fail closed unless receipt.outputSha256 equals that digest and matches the complete/non-complete rule.

findings.scenario: Timeout only reject()s the wrapper promise; the default AbortController is never aborted, and the caller signal is not aborted on duration-exceeded. propose: () => new Promise(() => { /* later mutate/I/O */ }) still runs after the executor has already returned budget-exhausted/cancelled. Termination is wait-side only; proposal work remains reachable.
findings.remediation: Create an internal AbortController, pass AbortSignal.any([caller, internal]), abort it on timeout/cancel/return, and do not treat unexported control errors thrown by propose as cancel/duration.

findings.scenario: Duration uses wall-clock setTimeout(maxDurationMs) while start/stop use options.now ?? Date.now. Frozen now() plus a slow async propose yields budget-exhausted despite 0 logical elapsed; now() jumping after a sync propose yields budget-exhausted without the timer. Deterministic injected clocks do not own the bound.
findings.remediation: Drive both the watchdog and elapsed check from the same clock (injectable now + injectable scheduler), and treat elapsed >= maxDurationMs as exhausted.

findings.scenario: deadlineAt is enforced only when startedAtMs > Date.parse(deadlineAt). A job with deadlineAt = start+1ms, maxDurationMs = 5000, and a propose that resolves at start+100ms still returns complete after the deadline.
findings.remediation: Reject deadline-expired if either startedAtMs or stoppedAtMs is past deadlineAt, before emitting complete.

findings.line: completeReceipt startedAt/stoppedAt:72-73 and schema stoppedAt < startedAt
findings.scenario: If now() is non-monotonic (NTP) or returns NaN/Infinity, new Date(...).toISOString() throws or AiTeammateRunReceiptV1Schema.parse throws on stoppedAt < startedAt. No terminal receipt is emitted.
findings.remediation: Clamp/validate timestamps; if stop < start or they are non-finite, return budget-exhausted/failed instead of throwing.

findings.line: Object.isFrozen(parsedJob) in complete-path propose; never-resolving Promise.race
findings.scenario: The complete test expects Object.isFrozen(job) but the executor never freezes job, so that assertion fails on standard Zod. The never-resolving case races a 5ms setTimeout against a 100ms wall-clock guard and does not assert hashes, freeze, or retryEligible. Green proof of freeze/immutability is not an oracle for the criterion.
findings.remediation: Freeze job in production code; assert nested freeze and binding against the original job; use a fake scheduler for duration tests.

audit.proof_assessment: The evidence file is not authority. GREEN claims 55 passing tests including Object.isFrozen on Zod .readonly() jobs/receipts; Zod object .readonly() is type-level and executor only shallow-freezes the result wrapper, so those assertions should fail unless an unshown runtime freeze exists. GREEN also runs registry.test.ts (not in this diff) and an unspecified prohibited-capability scan. Treat the slice as unverified except by static reading.
residual_risks: Injected propose is unsandboxed; network/fs/provider effects are possible inside the callback and are not intercepted.
Invalid jobs fail AiTeammateJobV1Schema.parse by throw rather than a rejected receipt (no bindable job).
Input is hashed/cloned before maxInputBytes is applied, so oversized payloads still pay CPU/memory.
Duration equality uses > in the post-check and setTimeout(maxDurationMs) in the watchdog, so the exact bound can complete or exhaust depending on race.
